answer: Proof-of-Timing Enrollment. An agent joins only when its request cadence passes a challenge: it must show a natural rise to and fall from a traffic nadir within a random interval, proving idle scheduling rather than scripted bursts. Each new identity pays a fixed latency tax—hours of forced silence during a bridge window before activation. An attacker running many sock-puppet agents pays that silence per identity, multiplying wall-clock time linearly while honest agents amortize it across a sparrow’s occasional long gap.
